creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Split off from `stop-the-checker` (a_25Nhy9Un4), which landed the other
false positives in that cluster. Deferred deliberately: it is a different
size class from the rest.

`index_of` returns `int?`, and an `in` membership guard doesn't narrow it:

    if flag in args:
        idx = args.index_of(flag)
        use(idx + 1)          // RAD30002 on code that provably can't be null

One real script hit this ~10 times from a single flag-parsing idiom.

### Why it was deferred

Narrowing is keyed on `*Symbol` pointer identity and nothing else -
`Frame.bindings` is `map[*Symbol]rl.TypingT` (`rts/check/narrow.go:18`).
There is no expression key, no place key, no container/index relation
anywhere in the narrower. Every predicate handler starts by resolving an
`*rl.Identifier` to a Symbol, so `if x.foo != null:` and `if xs[0] != null:`
don't narrow either. Generalizing the key type means changing `With`,
`WithMany`, `Lookup`, `joinFrames`, `dropNarrowings` and
`closureOverridesForLambda` together.

Note the plain form already works, because there IS a symbol to key on:

    idx = args.index_of(flag)
    if idx != null:
        use(idx + 1)          // clean

So the gap is specifically a guard whose subject is a *different
expression* than the thing being refined.

### A cheaper design worth trying first

Rather than generalizing `Frame`, keep a stack of active guard condition
nodes: `walkIf` pushes the branch condition for the duration of the truthy
body. `refineBuiltinReturn` then strips the null from `index_of`'s `int?`
when an active guard is syntactically `<target> in <subject>` matching this
call's own arguments.

That reuses the extension point the sibling card already leaned on, and it
is shape-driven in the same way `typeOfCallOfIdent` (`narrow.go:382`)
already pattern-matches an exact call shape. It does not generalize to
`x.foo` narrowing - if that's wanted too, the expensive path is the honest
one.

### Watch out for

- The guard must not survive into a lambda defined in the body and called
  later; see `closureOverridesForLambda` for the existing analogue.
- `args.index_of(flag)` is a `*rl.VarPath` with a UFCS segment, not a
  `*rl.Call`, so the syntactic match has to handle both call forms.
- Needs a negative snapshot: a guard on a *different* container
  (`if flag in other: args.index_of(flag)`) must NOT narrow.
title: index_of isn't narrowed by an 'in' membership guard
